sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the medical instruments used for recording: (a) blood pressure (b) conduction of the heart beat.
questions.answer: (a) Sphygmomanometer. (b) Electrocardiograph (ECG).

questions.q: After organ transplantation, a patient should be given immunosuppressants. (a) Why? (b) Which cells of the immune system are responsible for the rejection?
questions.answer: (a) To prevent the body's immune system from rejecting the foreign organ as an antigen. (b) T-cells (cell-mediated immunity).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The heart beat originates at the ______. (b) Blood is a ______ connective tissue.
questions.answer: (a) SA node. (b) fluid.

questions.q: Match: (a) Platelets (b) Lymphocytes (c) RBC with (i) antibodies (ii) clotting (iii) oxygen transport.
Write the antigens and antibodies of blood group (a) A (b) O.
questions.answer: (a) Antigen A, antibody b. (b) No antigen, antibodies a and b.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) Arteries have valves. (b) Pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood.
questions.answer: (a) False. (b) True.

questions.q: Name the two types of lymphocytes and their site of development.
questions.answer: B-cells and T-cells, both developing in the bone marrow.

questions.q: Name the immunodeficiency disorders: (a) absence of both T- and B-cells from birth (b) caused by HIV.
questions.answer: (a) SCID. (b) AIDS.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write the main functions of B-cells and T-cells in the immune system.
questions.answer: B-cells produce antibodies to neutralise antigens (humoral immunity); T-cells recognise and destroy infected cells and antigens directly (cell-mediated immunity).

questions.q: Draw a diagrammatic structure of an antibody and label the specific antigen-binding site.
questions.answer: Y-shaped molecule of four polypeptide chains: two heavy and two light chains joined by disulphide bonds, with two antigen-binding sites at the tips of the arms (variable regions) and a constant stem region.

questions.q: Differentiate between artery and vein (two points).
questions.answer: An artery carries blood from the heart, has thick elastic walls and no valves; a vein carries blood to the heart, has thin walls and valves.

questions.q: What is double circulation?
questions.answer: The blood passes twice through the heart in one complete circulation: pulmonary (heart-lungs-heart) and systemic (heart-body-heart).

questions.q: Write the steps of blood clotting in short.
questions.answer: Platelets release thromboplastin; with Ca++ it converts prothrombin to thrombin; thrombin changes fibrinogen to fibrin, which entangles RBCs and forms a clot.

questions.q: Why is O called the universal donor and AB the universal recipient?
questions.answer: O has no antigens on its RBCs so it does not agglutinate in others; AB has no antibodies in the plasma so it can receive any group.

questions.q: Define immunity and an antigen.
questions.answer: Immunity is the body's ability to resist disease-causing agents; an antigen is any substance that stimulates the production of antibodies.

questions.q: Differentiate between active and passive immunity (two points).
questions.answer: Active: the body makes its own antibodies after infection or vaccination, long-lasting; passive: ready-made antibodies are injected (serum), short-lived.

questions.q: Name any two functions of the lymph.
questions.answer: Drains excess tissue fluid and transports fats absorbed from the intestine.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the conduction of the heart beat.
questions.answer: The wave starts at the SA node (pacemaker) in the right atrium, causing atrial contraction; it reaches the AV node, passes to the bundle of His and Purkinje fibres in the ventricular walls and causes ventricular systole.

questions.q: Explain the path of blood in double circulation with a flow chart.
questions.answer: Body → venae cavae → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary veins → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → body.

questions.q: Write any three differences between blood and lymph.
questions.answer: Blood has RBCs and haemoglobin and is red; lymph is colourless with no RBCs; blood has more plasma proteins and flows in closed vessels with a pumping heart; lymph has no pump.

questions.q: Describe the structural differences between arteries, veins and capillaries.
questions.answer: Arteries have thick elastic muscular walls and small lumen; veins have thin walls, valves and large lumen; capillaries have walls of a single layer of endothelium for exchange.

questions.q: Explain the blood groups and transfusion.
questions.answer: Antigens A and B on RBCs and antibodies in plasma give groups A, B, AB and O; mismatched transfusion causes agglutination; O is the universal donor and AB the universal recipient; Rh factor must also match.

questions.q: Describe the cells of the immune system and their functions.
questions.answer: Lymphocytes: B-cells make antibodies; T-cells recognise and destroy antigens; macrophages and monocytes engulf bacteria by phagocytosis.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the structure of the human heart and the cardiac cycle.
questions.answer: Four chambers (two atria, two ventricles) with tricuspid, bicuspid and semilunar valves; heart sounds lubb and dubb; the beat begins at the SA node, passes to the AV node, bundle of His and Purkinje fibres; atrial systole is followed by ventricular systole and a joint diastole.

questions.q: Describe the composition of blood and the functions of its components.
questions.answer: Plasma (water, proteins, nutrients, hormones) and cells: RBCs carry gases, WBCs defend, platelets help clotting; the table of counts, origin in bone marrow and haemopoiesis.

questions.q: Describe the mechanism of blood coagulation with a flow chart.
questions.answer: Injury; platelets release thromboplastin; thromboplastin + Ca++ convert prothrombin to thrombin; thrombin converts fibrinogen to fibrin; fibrin + RBCs form the clot.

questions.q: What is immunity? Describe its types and the role of vaccines.
questions.answer: Innate and acquired immunity (active and passive); vaccines contain weakened antigens that stimulate antibody production, e.g. BCG and DPT; anti-tetanus serum gives passive immunity.

questions.q: Describe the disorders of blood and heart.
questions.answer: Hypertension, atherosclerosis (atheroma), arteriosclerosis, their causes and treatments such as angioplasty and bypass; immunodeficiency disorders SCID and AIDS.
